title: The vertical video takeover is here
summary: All major social and media platforms are converging around vertical video as their primary content format, a shift from their historically distinct identities. The article traces how platforms like YouTube, Instagram, and Netflix once had separate niches but are now unified by vertical video's dominance. This convergence reflects fundamental changes in how audiences consume content and the strategic decisions platforms are making to remain relevant.
content:
This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on all things vertical video, follow David Pierce. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here.
How it started
For a while, every social and media platform had its own identity. YouTube was for clips of TV shows and movies, and the home of so many members of a burgeoning creator community. Instagram was mostly pictures. Netflix was trying to be the on-demand HBO. Facebook was about friends. Twitter was about news. Snapchat was a messaging app.

zh.title: 竖屏视频已全面占领
zh.summary: 所有主要社交和媒体平台都在围绕竖屏视频进行整合,将其作为主要内容格式,这是一个重大转变,背离了它们各自的历史特色。文章追踪了YouTube、Instagram和Netflix等平台的演变过程,它们曾各具特色,如今却被竖屏视频的主导地位所统一。这种融合反映了观众内容消费方式的根本变化,以及各平台为保持相关性所做的战略决策。

title: Monday.com is the latest tech company to blame AI for layoffs — here are 20 others
summary: Monday.com becomes the latest tech company to attribute layoffs to AI adoption, joining at least 20 other major tech firms that have made similar announcements this year. The pattern reflects ongoing industry debates about whether automation concerns justify workforce reductions.
content: A running look — in reverse chronological order — at the bigger tech companies that have announced significant layoffs this year with AI as a stated factor.
